title: BSU vs EWU: tuition, size, location
summary: Boise State University (BSU) versus Eastern Washington University (EWU). Also searched as EWU vs BSU. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Boise State University and Eastern Washington University are both public institutions, but they differ in several key aspects. Boise State University, located in Boise, has a significantly larger undergraduate enrollment of 17,674 students compared to Eastern Washington University's 6,222 students in Cheney. Tuition for in-state students at Boise State is slightly higher, costing $9,048 annually, whereas Eastern Washington charges $8,586. These differences reflect variations in campus size and cost of attendance between the two universities.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing the cost of attendance at Boise State University (BSU) and Eastern Washington University (EWU), BSU's in-state tuition is $9,048, which is marginally higher than EWU's $8,586. For out-of-state students, BSU charges $27,788, while EWU's tuition is slightly lower at $25,959. Regarding student debt, the median debt for graduates who completed their programs at BSU is $20,500, compared to $19,500 at EWU. These figures illustrate that while BSU generally has higher tuition rates, the difference in median debt upon completion is relatively small between the two institutions.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Boise State University (BSU) and Eastern Washington University (EWU) offer distinct learning environments reflective of their campus settings and student populations. BSU, situated in Boise, Idaho, supports a larger undergraduate body with 17,674 students, fostering a more extensive campus community. In contrast, EWU, located in Cheney, Washington, enrolls 6,222 undergraduates, providing a smaller campus atmosphere. Both universities deliver their programs through traditional on-campus learning models, emphasizing in-person instruction and campus engagement. The differences in enrollment size and campus location contribute to varied student experiences at BSU versus EWU.

sections.heading: Pick BSU if
paragraphs: Pick Boise State University (BSU) if you prefer a public institution with a high admission rate and a moderate completion rate. BSU has an admission rate of 87.21%, making it accessible to a broad range of applicants. The university charges $9,048 annually for in-state tuition, which is competitive for public universities. Additionally, BSU's completion rate within 150% of the expected time is 60.2%, indicating a solid track record of student success. These factors make BSU a suitable choice for students seeking an affordable public university with a supportive academic environment.

sections.heading: Pick EWU if
paragraphs: Pick Eastern Washington University (EWU) if you are looking for a public institution with a very high admission rate, as EWU admits approximately 90.75% of applicants, making it highly accessible. The university offers in-state tuition at $8,586 annually, which is lower than many comparable public universities. However, prospective students should consider that EWU has a completion rate of about 43.49% within 150% of the expected time, which is lower than some other institutions. These factors suggest that EWU may be a good fit for students seeking an affordable and accessible public university experience.
